title: A platform-owned product can help today's customer while changing tomorrow's choice set
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34135 field experiment and model-based counterfactuals on Amazon private labels
geography: United States online retail; selected Amazon product categories

denominator.unit: randomized field experiment on Amazon shoppers and selected product categories

similar_product_substitution.value: consumers chose products similar along most observable dimensions

observations.method: Field experiment hiding Amazon-owned brands, with observed shopping and choice outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The experiment covers selected categories and short-run behavior; it does not measure long-run seller entry, exit, platform dependence, or all customer groups.
observations.subgroup: Amazon shoppers and products in the tested categories
observations.counterinterpretation: Similar observable products can still differ in unmeasured fit, trust, delivery, return experience, or brand value.

category_heterogeneity.value: consumer-surplus reductions exceeded 10% in some categories and were much smaller in others

demotion_welfare_gain.unit: estimated consumer-surplus effect of demoting private labels in search

observations.method: Model-based counterfactuals calibrated to the field experiment and heterogeneous consumer preferences.
observations.uncertainty: Consumer-surplus estimates depend on model specification, selected categories, short-run substitution, and the assumption that observed preferences transport to the counterfactual.
observations.subgroup: Consumers and categories represented in the experiment
observations.counterinterpretation: A short-run consumer benefit from availability or prominence does not establish fair ranking, durable seller competition, or long-run consumer welfare.

related_sources.claim: NBER supplies the field experiment, search/substitution results, and model-based short-run welfare estimates.
Separate FTC/state Amazon marketplace case supplies an institutional platform-control comparator; it is not pooled with the experiment.

boundary: This record separates product availability, search placement, observed substitution, search effort, cross-platform substitution, and model-based short-run consumer surplus. It does not establish long-run seller entry or exit, platform self-preferencing, data use, future prices, product quality, durable consumer dependence, or household welfare.
